text: The world's first webcam was watching a coffee pot.
Cambridge University, 1991. One computer lab, one shared coffee pot.
say: Cambridge University, nineteen ninety one. One computer lab, one shared coffee pot.

text: For some staff, getting coffee meant climbing several flights of stairs.
And often, the pot was already empty when they got there.
So two researchers pointed a camera at it, and wrote a small program in about a day.
A tiny black and white picture of the pot, on their screens, updated about three times a minute.
Pot empty? Stay at your desk.
In November 1993, it went on the World Wide Web. Now anyone online could check a coffee pot in England.
say: In November, nineteen ninety three, it went on the World Wide Web. Now anyone online could check a coffee pot in England.

text: Hundreds of thousands of people looked at it.
In 2001 the lab moved buildings. The camera was switched off, and one of the pots sold on eBay for £3,350.
say: In two thousand and one, the lab moved buildings. The camera was switched off, and one of the pots sold on eBay for three thousand, three hundred and fifty pounds.

text: The lesson? That camera answered one question: is it worth the trip?
Your website should too. Hours, prices, what's in stock, before they get in the car.
